scope: Read-only portability review of 27 new controls before normal Linux/macOS/Windows native-wheel selection.
facts: 26 cases do not require symlink creation or POSIX permission denial; permission and iteration failures are explicit monkeypatched exceptions.
Mutation controls write actual files and set a deliberate 1 ms directory mtime difference, rather than relying on scheduler timing.
Directory replacement controls close ordinary file writes before rename and retain the old directory, preventing immediate file-ID reuse in the owned fixture.
The actual signed publisher control explicitly creates POSIX runtime directory with 0700; on Windows the production private-state binding handles its private directory repair and validation.
The symlink refusal control already catches OSError from owned symlink creation and skips. A runner lacking symlink privilege therefore may execute only 26 new controls, which must remain explicit.
limitations: No Windows or macOS execution was performed in this review.
No assertion or skip was changed.
A skipped symlink control is not cross-platform proof of the symlink rejection path.
The publisher control uses an explicit ACK double; it does not authenticate a real native process or prove installed readiness.
